items.title: OpenAI slows Astra model over cyber risks
points: Internal tests flagged "critical" cyber capabilities in the unreleased Astra model, triggering OpenAI's 2023 preparedness framework (a formal safety protocol requiring extra safeguards when a model shows dangerous advanced abilities).
Stricter controls now include isolated testing environments and monitoring for agentic uses (tasks where an AI acts autonomously to reach a goal).
First public instance of a major AI lab slowing a model's development over cyber vulnerabilities; the model was not tied to the recent Hugging Face exploits.
Release timeline is uncertain until tighter security requirements are met.

items.title: Cloudflare launches Kitesurf, a browser built for AI agents
points: Kitesurf is a cloud-hosted browser designed for AI agents rather than humans, built in 12 weeks on Cloudflare's serverless Workers platform (code that runs on demand without managing servers).

Drops visual features like tabs and extensions, optimizing instead for context windows (how much text an AI can consider at once), token costs (charges based on input/output length), and prompt injection attacks (hidden commands smuggled into content to hijack an AI).
Uses less CPU and memory than Chromium for tasks like screenshots and HTML extraction, and has passed over 215,000 web platform compatibility tests.
Free during beta as part of Cloudflare's Browser Run service.

items.title: US sanctions Iran-linked crypto exchanges
points: Treasury sanctioned exchanges Shelbit and Aban Tether for moving money outside traditional banks and funding the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (an Iranian military entity).
IRGC-linked wallets sent over $1 million to Shelbit and received over $2 million back; Aban Tether processed millions with sanctioned Iranian exchanges Nobitex, Wallex, Bitpin, and Ramzinex.
Individual Siavash Kayvanpour and his firms in Georgia, Poland, and the UAE were also sanctioned; wallets he controls sent over $2 million to Nobitex, Iran's largest crypto exchange.

items.title: Flock pitched turning ride-share dashcams into a surveillance network
points: Plan would convert hundreds of thousands of Uber, Lyft, and delivery driver dashcams into mobile license-plate scanners as drivers work.
Relied on a partnership with dashcam maker Nexar covering roughly 350,000 devices; Flock says it pitched the idea to customers in August 2025 but never executed the deal.
Unlike Flock's stationary pole-mounted cameras, the mobile approach would greatly widen data collection, potentially without drivers' or ride-share companies' knowledge or consent.

items.title: Smaller items
points: Anthropic now lets separate Claude Code sessions message each other across macOS and Linux, so they can share findings and coordinate on shared projects.
Apple may raise iPhone 17 prices as soon as August 10, ahead of expected increases tied to next month's iPhone 18 Pro launch.

sections.title: OpenAI Slows Astra Model Over Cyber Security Concerns
points: Internal testing flagged 'critical' cyber capabilities in Astra, triggering OpenAI's 2023 preparedness framework (a formal safety protocol requiring enhanced safeguards for advanced AI risks).
Company is implementing stricter controls including isolated testing environments and monitoring for agentic uses (tasks where AI agents act autonomously to achieve goals).

sections.title: Cloudflare's Kitesurf Browser Built Specifically for AI Agents
points: Kitesurf is a cloud-hosted browser designed for AI agents rather than humans, built in just 12 weeks on Cloudflare's serverless Workers platform.

Eliminates visual features like tabs and extensions, instead optimizing for context windows (the amount of text an AI can consider at once), token costs (charges based on input/output length), and security threats like prompt injection attacks (attempts to manipulate AI by embedding hidden commands in user input).
Performance improvements: uses less CPU and memory than Chromium for tasks like screenshots and HTML extraction, and has passed over 215,000 web platform compatibility tests.
Currently free during beta phase as part of Browser Run service.

sections.title: US Imposes Sanctions on Iran-Linked Crypto Exchanges
points: Treasury sanctioned Shelbit and Aban Tether (Iran-based exchange) for facilitating money movement outside traditional banking and funding the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, an Iranian military entity.
Also sanctioned individual Siavash Kayvanpour and his associated firms in Georgia, Poland, and the UAE; wallets he controls sent over $2 million to Nobitex, Iran's largest crypto exchange.

Evidence shows IRGC-linked wallets transferred over $1 million to Shelbit and received over $2 million back, while Aban Tether processed millions in transactions with multiple sanctioned Iranian exchanges including Nobitex, Wallex, Bitpin, and Ramzinex.

sections.title: Flock's Proposed Mass Surveillance Plan Using Ride-Share Drivers
points: Flock planned to convert hundreds of thousands of Uber, Lyft, and delivery driver dashcams into mobile surveillance vehicles using their cameras to scan passing license plates while driving.
The scheme relied on a partnership with dashcam maker Nexar covering approximately 350,000 devices, though Flock claimed to never execute the deal it pitched to potential customers in August 2025.

Unlike Flock's standard pole-mounted cameras used in stationary scanning, this mobile approach would expand data collection scope significantly while potentially operating without driver or rideshare company knowledge.
The plan raised serious privacy and consent questions about using third-party drivers for surveillance without their explicit awareness or consent.
